title: Eval scenario
description: One deterministic scenario inside an eval suite: which deployed profile it targets, how the agent is invoked, and the repository-owned evaluator that asserts on observable outcomes. The evaluator's exit code is the whole assertion protocol — 0 pass, 1 assertion failure, anything else evaluator/harness error — so a broken evaluator is never reported as a misbehaving agent. Complex polling and evidence checks belong in the evaluator script, not in new YAML fields.

name.description: Unique within the suite (the runner enforces uniqueness across scenarios; the schema cannot see siblings).

profile.description: The deployed profile this scenario addresses — resolved against the onboarded catalogue, never an implicit global agent.

prompt.description: Path (relative to the scenario directory, contained within it) to a prompt file the runner sends to the profile before the evaluator runs; the response lands at $HG_EVAL_RESPONSE. Omit when the evaluator owns the invocation itself (webhook, relay, cron).

evaluate.description: Path (relative to the scenario directory, contained within it) to the deterministic evaluator executable. Repository-owned code: untrusted (cloned) sources require --allow-repo-scripts.

timeout.description: Hard wall-clock budget in seconds for one run, prompt included. Defaults to the suite's, then 300.

repeat.description: Runs per invocation, each recorded independently — for surfacing nondeterminism by hand, not for retry-until-green.

required.description: Defaults to true. false makes the scenario informational: it runs and reports but never fails the suite.

setup.description: Shell commands run in order from the scenario directory before each run. Repository-owned code, trust-gated like `evaluate`.

cleanup.description: Shell commands run from the scenario directory after each run — ALWAYS, including on timeout and evaluator crash.
